family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the class-status ladder the card leaves out: suspension of class - what triggers it (overdue survey, unrectified Condition of Class, unreported casualty), whether it is automatic or discretionary - against withdrawal of class as permanent termination, and the consequence chain from each to statutory certificates, insurance cover and trading.
family_decisions.why: The card defines Conditions of Class and Memoranda but never mentions suspension, and mentions withdrawal only in passing in the CE-relevance prose. Three examiners asked this - the highest recurrence in the enrichment set.

family_decisions.evidence: QB1_A#q5 'CLC - Civil Liability Convention' opens: 'CLC 1969 was adopted after the Torrey Canyon disaster (1967). The CLC 1992 Protocol (superseding 1969 for contracting states)...' - the 69-vs-92 distinction the family asks for is already the card's first heading.
family_decisions.why: The ask 'CLC 69 and CLC 92' was targeted at the P&I card QB1_A#q1, which mentions CLC only in a covered-perils list. The corpus holds six CLC-bearing cards; QB1_A#q5 already answers the ask.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the distinction between root cause and proximate cause: root cause is the engineering end-point of the RCA the card already performs, while proximate cause is the insurance and legal test of the dominant, effective cause of the loss, and it is proximate cause - not root cause - that decides which policy responds.
family_decisions.why: The card already has a full 'Root Cause Analysis (RCA) & Technical Investigation' section but never mentions proximate cause, so it answers half the ask. Two examiners asked it.

family_decisions.missing_limb: State the MGO/MDO carbon factor and explain the counter-intuitive part the examiner was probing: why the distillate's Cf (about 3.206) is HIGHER than HFO's (3.114) even though MGO is the cleaner fuel - because Cf tracks carbon mass fraction, and HFO's sulphur, ash and asphaltenes dilute its carbon per tonne.
family_decisions.why: The card gives Cf for HFO and methanol and explains the 44/12 ratio, but never states the MGO figure the examiner quoted, and nowhere explains why a cleaner fuel can carry a higher factor. Two examiners asked it.

family_decisions.evidence: QB4_F#q5 'Cyber security - basic principles' carries the heading 'Basic Principles - The 5-Step Framework' and sets out Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover with shipboard examples, under ISM 1.2.2, MSC.428(98) and MSC-FAL.1/Circ.3. Those five ARE the functional elements asked for.
family_decisions.why: The ask 'Explain all the functional requirements of Cyber security' was targeted at QB4_F#q6, the LRIT-and-AIS card, which has no cyber content. The correct card sits one anchor away in the same file and already answers it in full.

The family's ask text is the literal string 'Q Nov 2023 1 3' - a source citation, not an examiner ask. As with GAP-0364, no limb can be stated, so rule 10 forces a HOLD. Recurrence of 2 does not rescue an unreadable ask.

The ask is the fragment 'TIO2 APPLICATION' filed against the MS Act versus RPSL card. Titanium dioxide has no relationship to Indian manning legislation, and the fragment is too short to identify whether it means a cargo, a coating or something else. Both the target and the ask fail, so no limb can be stated.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the hull deformation vocabulary a surveyor uses and how each is assessed: buckling, set-in/dishing of plating, tripping of stiffeners and permanent set - what causes each, how the extent is measured against class allowable deformation, and what makes it a Condition of Class.
family_decisions.why: The Hull survey card covers survey types, close-up scope and UTM but never names or grades a deformation defect, which is what 'hull malformation' asks.

'Hull texturing' has no established meaning in hull survey practice; it could mean coating texture/roughness, surface preparation profile, or be a transcription of another term. Rule 10 forbids inventing a limb, and this family was silently clustered with GAP-0075 into one action despite being a different subject.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Explain that 'A' is the division class and the number is its insulation rating in minutes: an A-class division is steel or equivalent, suitably stiffened, capable of preventing the passage of smoke and flame for a 60-minute standard fire test, while the A-60/A-30/A-15/A-0 suffix states how long insulation holds the unexposed face within the permitted temperature rise - so A-0 is still an A division with no insulation requirement.
family_decisions.why: The card holds A-60 as a figure but never defines an A-class division or explains what the suffix measures, which is exactly the difference asked for.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Bring the Seafarer Medical Fitness Certificate section up to date: state the current medical examination standard and certificate validity position, and the most recent change to it beyond the gender-marker change the examiner set aside.
family_decisions.why: The card's medical certificate section cites the ILO/WHO guidelines generically with no date, no validity period and no amendment position, so it cannot answer a question framed as 'the latest change'.
family_decisions.currentness_note: The whole value of this limb is its currency; it must be researched, not reasoned.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the objectives half of the ask - why GBS was needed at all: IMO wanted to set and audit the safety goal rather than write construction rules itself, after prescriptive rules alone proved unable to prevent structural losses, so Tier III audit of class rules replaces IMO rule-writing.
family_decisions.why: The card explains the five tiers and the scope precisely but never states an objective or a rationale, and the ask puts OBJECTIVES, WHY NEEDED in capitals.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Put figures behind the promise the card already makes: MLC Title 3 accommodation minima - berth internal dimensions, headroom, floor area per seafarer and door sill/coaming heights - as numbers a candidate can quote.
family_decisions.why_old_wrong: QB4_E#q3 is the young-seafarer card (minimum age, night work, hazardous work). Accommodation dimensions apply to every seafarer and have nothing to do with age.
family_decisions.why_new_right: QB4_C#q6's Title 3 entry literally reads 'Specifies structural dimensions for cabins, mess rooms...' and then gives no dimension. It is the MLC card, and the examiner asked 'as per MLC' - which the Indian MS Act card QB1_F#q12 would answer only at one remove.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the ME-GI as the missing member of the comparison: high-pressure direct gas injection on the diesel cycle, contrasted with the ME-GA's low-pressure Otto-cycle admission - and how combustion actually proceeds in each, which is what makes their methane-slip behaviour differ.
family_decisions.why: The card compares the ME-GA against four-stroke low-pressure Otto engines. ME-GI, which the examiner named, does not appear in it, so the LNG engine-type question cannot be answered from this card.
family_decisions.matching_note: ME-GI and ME-GA tokenise to nothing under the corpus tokeniser, which is why lexical coverage scoring never surfaced this.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add who actually performs an IMSAS audit and where India stands: the audit is conducted by auditors nominated by other Member States and coordinated through the IMO Secretariat on a fixed cycle, and India's own audit position under that cycle.
family_decisions.why: The card sets out the III Code's flag, coastal and port State obligations and its mandatory status under SOLAS XIII, but names no auditor and gives India no status, which are two of the examiner's six asks.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add who carries freight-market risk under a Contract of Affreightment and how: the owner commits tonnage over a period at an agreed rate and so is exposed if the market rises, the shipper secures capacity and is exposed if it falls - which is why a CoA is a hedging instrument as much as a carriage contract.
family_decisions.why: The card positions the CoA precisely in the chartering spectrum and describes the volume-contract mechanics, but says nothing about risk allocation, which is the examiner's second word.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the instrument-type ladder the card never defines: convention, protocol, annex, regulation, code, and guideline or circular - which of them bind, and how a code becomes mandatory by being referenced from a convention regulation.
family_decisions.why: The card explains how an instrument is adopted and how consent is expressed, but never what the different kinds of instrument ARE, which is the difference the examiner asked for.
family_decisions.avoid_duplication: The Indian Act-versus-Rules half of this vocabulary is already owned by QB9_D#q9 ('Act vs rule - difference in Indian legal context'). Cross-link; do not restate it.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add how a CoP is actually obtained, as against what it is: the approved training and assessment route, who may issue or endorse it, the evidence the Administration requires, and which CoPs carry a refresher obligation.
family_decisions.why: At 1,203 characters this is the second-shortest target in the set. It defines both certificates and lists CoP examples but never states an issuance criterion for either, which is the ask.
family_decisions.unresolved: The examiner's 'DC criteria' cannot be expanded with confidence - DC is not an established abbreviation in this context - so the limb is deliberately scoped to CoP issuance only and DC must be clarified before production.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the qualifying sea service TEAP requires for an engineer officer to sit for and obtain each level of CoC - the national sea-service rule the card's own framework exists to set out.
family_decisions.why: The card explains what TEAP is, why India needs it and where it sits under the MS Act 2025 Part IV, but states no sea-service requirement for any rank, which is the ask.
family_decisions.unverifiable_citation: The examiner's 'III/16' is not a valid STCW regulation - Chapter III runs III/1 to III/7 - so the citation must not be reproduced.
family_decisions.co_author_with: ENR-035 - both concern qualifying sea service for an engineer CoC, one from the STCW side and one from the TEAP side. Author together so the two cards agree.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the rung below the one the card starts at: the STCW Regulation III/1 entry requirements for an engineer officer of the watch - the qualifying supervised watchkeeping sea service and the 750 kW propulsion-power threshold - so the ladder up to the III/2 3,000 kW certificate the card already explains is complete.
family_decisions.why: The card is built in four layers from the III/2 certificate upward and never mentions III/1 or 750 kW, so a candidate asked to describe the progression from below cannot answer from it.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add what AVD actually is and how it works: an aqueous dispersion of exfoliated vermiculite that, applied to a burning cell, leaves a non-conductive ceramic-like encapsulating layer which cools, isolates and blocks cell-to-cell propagation - and how it is applied relative to the boundary cooling the card already prescribes.
family_decisions.why: The card explains thermal runaway chemistry and boundary cooling but never mentions AVD, which the examiner named explicitly and asked for both materials and method.
family_decisions.merged_note: Authorisation records this family as merging GAP-0223 (alternative chemistries, plasma).

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the contents-verification and pressure limbs the card omits: how a CO2 cylinder is checked by weighing against its stamped tare weight and the loss that triggers refilling, why that differs from the ultrasonic liquid-level method the examiner contrasted it with, the stored pressure at reference temperature expressed in Pa as asked, and the low-pressure/leak alarm arrangement.
family_decisions.why: The card is entirely about the hydrostatic test interval regime under MSC.1/Circ.1318/Rev.1. It contains no weighing method, no stored pressure and no leak alarm - three separate numeric limbs the examiner pressed.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the Load Line timber deck cargo numeric criteria the card omits - the permitted extent and height of the deck stow and the reckoning point used in the timber freeboard assignment - so the candidate can answer with figures rather than with the general TDC Code stability criteria the card already gives.
family_decisions.why: The card gives GM0, GZ area and Timber Load Line assignment but carries none of the geometric stow criteria the examiner quoted.
family_decisions.evidence_caution: The candidate-reported figures ('33 PERC NT ON DECK', '500M OR 2SHIP LENGTH FRM FRWD TO RECKONING POINT') are a garbled recollection and must be verified against ICLL Annex I Chapter III before anything is written. If they cannot be substantiated the limb reduces to the stow-extent criteria only.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Explain what the SDR actually is and why the figure moves: an IMF basket unit (USD, EUR, CNY, JPY, GBP), valued daily, with the basket composition and weights reviewed on a fixed multi-year cycle - so a convention limit fixed in SDR is not fixed in any national currency.
family_decisions.why: The card quotes 100/115/250 million SDR limits but never says what an SDR is or what makes it move, which is precisely the ask.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Say who the average adjuster is and what qualifies them: an independent professional appointed by the shipowner, in practice a Fellow of the Association of Average Adjusters, and why that independence matters to the parties whose contributions they assess.
family_decisions.why: All three GA cards name the adjuster but none state qualification or appointment. QB1_A#q9 is the fullest GA card and the only one with a Procedure heading that already lists 'Average Adjuster appointed (Lloyd's Average Adjuster or equivalent)' - the limb attaches there.
family_decisions.duplicate_home_note: Three cards own General Average (QB1_A#q9, QB9_A#q4, QB1_B#q14) - duplicate-home debt not recorded in the authorisation's two known pairs.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Distinguish a marine-insurance warranty from a guarantee: a warranty is a term the assured must comply with exactly, breach of which suspends the insurer's liability from the moment of breach until remedied (Marine Insurance Act 1906 s.33 as reformed by the Insurance Act 2015, which replaced automatic discharge with suspension), whereas a guarantee is a third party's separate promise to answer for performance or defect.
family_decisions.why: QB1_B#q19 is the corpus's insurance-principles card (breach of the implied warranty of seaworthiness, privity, denial of claims) and is the only home for the distinction; a corpus search finds no dedicated warranty card - only QB3_A#q10 unsafe-vs-unseaworthy.
family_decisions.currentness_note: The Insurance Act 2015 reform is the trap - a card that states the pre-2015 automatic-discharge rule would be wrong.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Say where an approved component's identification is physically found on the part (the stamped/engraved component number on the cylinder liner and equivalent marking on other listed components) and who issues that number - the engine maker, recorded in the approved components list, which the surveyor matches part-to-file.
family_decisions.why: The card lists the approved components list as NTF content and says the surveyor checks it, but never says where the number is on the part or who originates it, which is the whole ask.

family_decisions.missing_limb: State what actually caps on-deck tier height, since the candidate's 'as per the loading and bay plan' answer names the output rather than the rule: the CSM's approved stack height and stack weight limits, lashing and twistlock capacity, wind heeling and stability, and the navigating-bridge line-of-sight requirement - with the bay plan as the result of those limits.
family_decisions.why: The card covers the CSM, CSAP and lashing certification but gives no tier limit and no derivation, which is the examiner's follow-up.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the operator-initiated fuel-mode changeover procedure in both directions - gas to diesel and diesel to gas - including the purge and ramp sequence and what must be confirmed before and after, as distinct from the automatic 40 percent LEL trip the card already describes.
family_decisions.why: The card covers the automatic gas trip and fallback to diesel thoroughly but contains no manual changeover procedure, which is what the examiner asked for.
family_decisions.scope_note: The ask's LPG liquefaction and stage-temperature limb is cargo-plant content and is deliberately excluded to keep this edit coherent.

family_decisions.evidence: QB1_A#q24 'Casualty Investigation Code' carries Code and Purpose (MSC.255(84), 2008), Definitions, Reporting Chain, the no-blame Critical Firewall and Human Element Factors. QB1_B#q15, QB4_G#q6, QB4_B#q6 and QB5_B#q16 cover it further.
family_decisions.why: The ask 'Casualty Inv. Code details' was targeted at QB1_C#q7 'Structural damage - assessment and reporting', which is a damage-response card and does not own the Casualty Investigation Code at all.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add Bloom's taxonomy as the framework for setting onboard training objectives at rising cognitive levels - remember, understand, apply, analyse, evaluate, create - and show how the level chosen dictates both the delivery method and the assessment used.
family_decisions.why_old_wrong: QB4_J#q8 is 'What are the different types of leadership'. Bloom's taxonomy is a learning-objectives framework, not a leadership style; it shares no subject with that card.
family_decisions.why_new_right: QB5_C_A#q7 'On-board training - how do you design and deliver it step by step' is the corpus's training-design card, which is where a taxonomy of learning objectives belongs.

family_decisions.evidence: The target card carries a dedicated heading 'Section 62 Mandate (formerly Section 95 of the repealed 1958 Act)' whose body cites Section 62 (Part V) of the Merchant Shipping Act 2025 as the express power to regulate recruitment and placement, and its CE Relevance names the DGS as the issuer of the RPSL registration.
family_decisions.why: All three limbs of the ask - who approves, why it is needed, and where RPS sits in the MS Act - are answered on the card itself. The authorisation recorded the section citation as missing after the card had already been updated from the repealed s.95 to s.62.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the GHG Protocol Scope 1/2/3 decomposition and map it onto the boundary distinction the card already draws: Scope 1 direct emissions from fuel burned on board, Scope 2 purchased energy such as shore power, Scope 3 the value chain including upstream fuel production - and note that Scope 1/2/3 is corporate accounting whereas tank-to-wake versus well-to-wake is regulatory accounting.
family_decisions.why: The card's 'Boundary Trap' section handles tank-to-wake against well-to-wake well, but the string 'Scope 1', 'Scope 2' and 'Scope 3' does not appear anywhere in it. The examiner asked in the corporate-accounting vocabulary.

The family's ask text is the literal string 'SAJEEEV QUESTIONS' - a source placeholder, not an examiner ask. No identifiable limb can be stated, so rule 10 forces a HOLD rather than an invented enrichment of the London Convention card.

The ask is 'Abbreviations of code and conventions' - a recall probe, not a content gap. The card already expands CLC, the Fund Convention and MARPOL Annex I in full at first use, and an abbreviations list is not an examiner-relevant limb of an oil-tanker liability answer. It fails the candidate-value test in rule 23.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the human-element escalation ladder as a graded sequence - counselling and informal correction, formal warning and disciplinary action under the company procedure, and targeted retraining - and state what determines which rung is right.
family_decisions.why: The card's CE-actions-in-order list is a complaint-handling sequence (stop it, record it, inform the Master, use the MLC 5.1.5 procedure). Counselling, discipline and training appear only three times across 8,013 characters and never as a graded response.

family_decisions.evidence: The target card's own 'CE's Post-Casualty Obligations' section already closes the loop: evidence preservation, witness statement, ISM root cause analysis pushed beyond individual error to systemic factors, then 'Corrective action: must fix the root cause, not the symptom - replacing a failed valve is not enough; also fix the PMS interval that missed it and train crew on early warning signs'.
family_decisions.why: The authorisation recorded 'closing the loop from an injury report to a preventive control' as missing from a 5,713-character card whose closing section is exactly that loop.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Place the drill on the strategic/tactical axis the examiner used: the SOPEP and the company response policy are the strategic layer, the drill is the tactical layer that rehearses and tests it - and say what each layer is meant to prove.
family_decisions.why: The card sets out OPRC, SOPEP, SMPEP and the high-seas action and reporting sequence, but frames nothing in strategic-against-tactical terms, so a candidate cannot answer the framing the examiner imposed.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Enumerate what the ICOF supplement carries besides the list of cargoes: the ship type assignment, the tank-by-tank record of the containment and handling equipment fitted, and the carriage conditions each listed cargo depends on.
family_decisions.why: The card covers the certificate's core contents, issuer and survey cycle but treats the supplement as the cargo list only, which is precisely what the examiner excluded.

family_decisions.evidence: QB9_A#q8 'UNCLOS - explain in detail' opens with a full maritime-zone table (internal waters, territorial sea 0-12, contiguous 12-24, EEZ, continental shelf), then sovereignty vs jurisdiction and hot pursuit under Art 111. That is the salient-features answer.
family_decisions.why: The ask 'Salient features of UNCLOS' was targeted at QB1_A#q21, the narrow Innocent Passage card. Innocent passage is one feature; the overview card already exists elsewhere.

family_decisions.evidence: The target card carries the headings 'Ship Risk Profile (SRP) - How Ships Get Selected for Inspection' (High/Standard/Low Risk Ship, recalculated on a rolling basis across Paris, Tokyo and Indian Ocean MoUs) and 'Where Ships and Authorities Check the Risk Profile & Detention Record'. Those are the ask's two limbs verbatim.
family_decisions.why: The authorisation recorded the risk profile and the targeting data source as missing from a 7,054-character card that has a dedicated section for each. This family also absorbed GAP-0402 and GAP-0404, so the downgrade clears three source families.

family_decisions.evidence: QB4_B#q14 'How do you approach mentoring a Junior Engineer throughout a voyage? What specific methods do you use?' is a dedicated development-methods card, supported by QB5_A#q15 (mentoring/reverse mentoring), QB5_A#q13 and QB9_H#q5 (appraisal), QB5_C_A#q7 (training design) and fourteen leadership/motivation cards.
family_decisions.why: 'Personality development onboard' has no distinct content beyond that cluster, and the authorised target was the Thomas-Kilmann conflict-management card, which is a different subject. Adding development content there would worsen the architecture, not improve coverage.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the owner's case for an alternative fuel expressed through the card's own quantity: because LCV sets the mass burned per unit of work, a low-carbon fuel's benefit must be stated per unit of ENERGY, not per tonne - and that is what decides bunker cost, tank capacity and compliance value to the owner.
family_decisions.why: The card is a rigorous LCV/HCV thermodynamics card with no commercial content at all. The examiner asked how the fuel profits the owner.
family_decisions.avoid_duplication: The carbon-per-unit-energy comparison itself is already made at QB6#q6 (methanol Cf 1.375 but CV 19.9 against HFO 40.2 MJ/kg, so mass roughly doubles). Cross-link to it rather than restating it - rule 20.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Draw the IGC/IGF boundary and say which instrument governs a gas-fuelled conversion: IGC governs the ship carrying the gas as CARGO, IGF governs the ship using low-flashpoint gas as FUEL - so a fossil-to-methane main engine retrofit on an LPG carrier is an IGF Code matter even though the ship is an IGC ship.
family_decisions.why: At 1,663 characters the card covers only tank types A/B/C and membrane. The IGF Code is not mentioned, so the code-boundary question the examiner led with has no answer here.
family_decisions.scope_note: The ask's retrofit advantages/disadvantages and owner-persuasion limbs are excluded - they are a commercial answer, not an IGC tank-type limb, and adding them would overload a short technical card (rule 19).

family_decisions.evidence: The target card's own Limb 3 is titled 'does a UV system meet US requirements?' and its 15-second answer states that the USCG judges living/dead by the FDA/CMFDA stain method rather than IMO's viable/non-viable MPN method, so a UV system needs a substantially higher dose - and calls that difference 'the whole point of the question'.
family_decisions.why: The authorisation recorded the IMO-versus-USCG comparison as missing, but the card was rebuilt during P0 production and now leads with exactly that comparison. The sibling family GAP-0065 on this same card was already dispositioned ALREADY_COVERED by the laptop; this one was not, and should have been.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add what changes when the handover is a change of MANAGEMENT rather than a change of chief engineer, scoped to a single intended voyage: no outgoing chief to hand over from, an unverified PMS and defect history, the DOC and SMS transition and interim certification, and how you triage what must be proved before that one voyage as against what can follow.
family_decisions.why: The card assumes a normal chief-to-chief handover throughout - it opens 'executing a formal, documented handover with the outgoing Chief'. Both the management-change scenario and the intended-voyage scoping the examiner insisted on are absent.

family_decisions.missing_limb: State the reporting route for containers lost at sea - which declaration/form carries it and to whom it is reported - and complete the FAL form list the card's own heading promises.
family_decisions.why: Card heading reads 'FAL Standardised Forms (9 Forms)' but the body enumerates only Forms 1-7, so the card cannot answer 'which FAL form reports loss of containers' and is internally inconsistent as it stands.
family_decisions.also: REQUIRED_CORRECTION_WITH_ENRICHMENT - the 9-vs-7 count mismatch is a live defect that the enrichment cannot be added around.

family_decisions.evidence: QB4_A#q16 answers the Maritime Labour Certificate, eligibility, validity and required surveys; QB4_A#q14 answers DMLC Part I and Part II - who issues each and what each contains; QB9_H#q4 covers grievance escalation. The 'what is different for a young seafarer' limb is the target card QB4_E#q3 itself.
family_decisions.why: Every limb of this multi-part ask is already owned by an existing card. It was clustered onto the young-seafarer card alongside the accommodation-dimensions family despite sharing no subject with it.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the two limbs the card lacks: the item-by-item scope of SOLAS Chapter XII beyond Reg 11 (what the chapter as a whole imposes on bulk carriers), and the stability criteria that must be satisfied after flooding, which the card names as a loadicator output without ever stating.
family_decisions.why: The card cites SOLAS XII Reg 11 and MSC.1/Circ.1229 but treats Chapter XII as a single carriage requirement, and mentions damage stability only as something the instrument calculates.
family_decisions.bloat_caution: The ask also contains a ballasting-versus-stress limb. The card already covers bending moment and shear force, so that limb is deliberately excluded to keep this one edit coherent.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the two Indian-specific limbs the card omits: the Merchant Shipping Act 2025 provision under which oil pollution prevention and spill reporting bite, cited by section, and the national reporting centre a ship actually calls or messages on discovering a spill in Indian waters.
family_decisions.why: The card explains the plan, the Coast Guard's coordinating role and the Tier I/II/III escalation but names no statute section and no reporting centre, which are two of the examiner's three explicit asks.
family_decisions.currentness_note: Section numbering must come from the Merchant Shipping Act 2025 in force 15 March 2026, not the 1958 Act.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the Indian seafarer welfare funding institutions the card omits - the Seamen's Provident Fund and the seafarers' welfare fund/board machinery, who contributes and what they pay for - and the COVID-era relief measures taken for stranded and repatriated seafarers.
family_decisions.why: The card covers Part V of the MS Act 2025 (accommodation, medical, MLC implementation) but names no welfare fund or provident fund at all, which is the whole of the ask.
family_decisions.currentness_note: Must establish whether the Seamen's Provident Fund Act 1966 survives the Merchant Shipping Act 2025 repeals - the repeal-tracking trap that caught the Coastal Shipping Act 2025 previously.
family_decisions.merged_note: Authorisation records this family as merging GAP-0533.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the electric propulsion drive train the azimuth pod hangs off: generator sets to main switchboard, transformer, frequency converter, propulsion motor and pod - and why diesel-electric is chosen for this arrangement.
family_decisions.why: The card describes Z-drive and L-drive mechanics and names an electric motor in the L-drive without ever explaining where its power comes from. A corpus search finds no electric-propulsion card anywhere, so this is the only home.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Name the ITU as the United Nations specialised agency for telecommunications and state its role behind the number the card already explains - allocation of the Maritime Identification Digits and call signs, and the Radio Regulations underpinning GMDSS.
family_decisions.why_old_wrong: QB2_A#q5 is 'Container lost at sea - CE actions'; it has no telecommunications content and no route to the ask.
family_decisions.why_new_right: QB6_F#q4 'What is MMSI, how is it structured, and where is it used onboard' is the card the laptop reason itself names ('reached through the MMSI and call-sign card').

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the maintenance-type taxonomy the card never names - planned/preventive, corrective/breakdown, condition-based and predictive, and where risk-based maintenance of critical equipment sits - so the candidate can answer 'type of maintenance' rather than describe only the PMS workflow.
family_decisions.why: The card answers where the PMS is mandated (ISM Code Section 10) and what records are kept, but contains no classification of maintenance types, which is the first of the examiner's three asks.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Give the ESP its regulatory citation - the SOLAS chapter and the ESP Code resolution that make it mandatory - which is the one part of this four-part ask the card does not answer.
family_decisions.why: The card already contains the Condition Evaluation Report, the thickness measurement reports and the survey cycle, so three of the four limbs are covered. It opens 'a mandatory survey regime under SOLAS' without ever naming the chapter, and the examiner asked for it explicitly.
family_decisions.note: At 1,349 characters this is the shortest target in the set; it can absorb the citation comfortably.

family_decisions.insertion: examiner chain entry on the drydock planning card
family_decisions.why: The ask is the two-word probe 'Surveys attended' - a personal-experience opener, not a content gap. The card already carries a 'Coinciding Surveys' section listing what falls due in a dock window, so no substantive limb is missing and a full answer edit would add nothing a candidate needs.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the tramp side of the contrast: no fixed schedule or published tariff, employed fixture by fixture under a charterparty rather than a liner bill of lading, freight negotiated per voyage against a market rate, and the different allocation of port, cargo-handling and delay risk that follows.
family_decisions.why: The card is the Liner/NVOCC/VOCC operational model and the word tramp appears once. The commercial contrast the examiner asked for is absent.

family_decisions.missing_limb: An entire post-collision response answer: immediate checks after a collision, watertight integrity assessment, the statutory and commercial reporting chain, and the document and record set to be preserved and submitted (VDR, logs, alarm printouts, soundings).
family_decisions.why: The authorised target QB5_B#q9 is CBDR - collision AVOIDANCE theory under COLREGS Rule 7. A corpus-wide search finds no post-collision response card at all: the only other collision hit is QB1_supplementary#q18, the collision BULKHEAD structural card. This ask cannot be an enrichment because no card owns the topic, and it is too large to be a limb.
family_decisions.escalation: New-card production is closed, so this stops here per rule 12. It means the final authorisation missed a genuine new-card need.
family_decisions.overlap_note: The ask's closing limb - who pays the 3/4 and who pays the remaining 1/4 - is the same missing limb as ENR-003/GAP-0616. If a card is later authorised, cross-link rather than restate.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the institutional and commercial response to recent maritime security incidents: the IMO's position and the instruments it has used, the flag State's role and advice to its ships, and the insurance consequence - war-risk listed areas, additional premium on transit, notice to underwriters and crew war-zone entitlements.
family_decisions.why: The card is the IMO Legal Committee response card (abandonment, fraudulent registries, MASS liability) so the IMO/flag-State half belongs here. The insurance half is absent corpus-wide: all nine war-risk/BMP5 cards contain zero insurance content.
family_decisions.currentness_note: Highest currentness risk in the set - a security-incident answer is stale within months.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Explain how the 3/4ths Running Down Clause actually operates rather than merely stating the fraction: the cross-liabilities basis of settlement, that it responds only to collision liability to the OTHER vessel, and that the residual quarter plus any excess over the insured value plus the heads RDC excludes (wreck removal, pollution, cargo on own ship, personal injury) all fall to P&I.
family_decisions.why: The examiner explicitly rejected the candidate's answer as 'only the first part' - the strongest available evidence of candidate failure. The card states Clause 8 as one line ('H&M covers 3/4 ... the 1/4 balance + any excess covered by P&I') and stops exactly where the examiner pressed.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Distinguish a plain bareboat/demise charter from a bareboat charter-cum-demise: the latter carries an ownership-transfer obligation at the end of the term, so the periodic payment includes a capital repayment element rather than pure hire - and identify the clause that effects the transfer.
family_decisions.why: The card treats bareboat and demise as one item in the chartering spectrum. The cum-demise variant, its payment mechanics and its transfer clause are absent, and no dedicated charter-types card exists in the corpus.
family_decisions.split_from: Clustered with GAP-0157 into one action although risk allocation and the bareboat-cum-demise structure are different limbs - rule 17.

family_decisions.missing_limb: State why the margin line sat where it did - 76 mm below the bulkhead deck at side as a deliberate reserve against progressive flooding over the bulkhead deck and loss of the evacuation route - so the candidate can explain the principle rather than only report that the 2009 amendments deleted it.
family_decisions.why: The card explains what the margin line was, that it was removed, and the modern replacement principle, but never the rationale the examiner asked for.
family_decisions.bloat_caution: This card is already 11,456 characters, the largest target in the set. The addition must be one or two sentences inside the existing Margin Line section, not a new section.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Separate what a class society does as class from what it does as a Recognised Organisation: classification work needs no delegation, whereas statutory certification is exercised only to the extent a particular flag has delegated it in its written RO agreement - so a single society's authority differs flag by flag, and some flags withhold specific certificates entirely.
family_decisions.why: The card states the criteria for becoming an RO but never states that RO authority is flag-specific and bounded, which is exactly the 'what can IRClass alone do and not do' ask.
family_decisions.source_note: The True Source RO Code holding is an image-only scan, so the RO Code text may not be quotable from the corpus and will need a primary fetch.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Add the pre-release controls for sending an LSA item (lifeboat davit / launching appliance) to a shore workshop: use of a maker-authorised or Administration-certificated service provider under MSC.402(96), the scope of work and certification returned, and the evidence the SEQ surveyor expects on completion.
family_decisions.why_old_wrong: QB10_B#q1 is the 2024-2028 SOLAS/MARPOL amendment overview; it does not own lifeboat davit repair control in any form.
family_decisions.why_new_right: QB1_E#q1 is the SEQ (Safety Equipment) survey card the laptop reason itself names ('the SEQ/LSA survey answer that already scores 0.60'); third-party LSA repair control is a limb of survey preparation.

family_decisions.evidence: QB1_A#q5 opens 'CLC 1969 was adopted after the Torrey Canyon disaster (1967). The CLC 1992 Protocol (superseding 1969 for contracting states) applies to tankers carrying persistent oil as cargo' and continues into the 1992 defences, compulsory insurance and the 2000 SDR limitation amendments.
family_decisions.why: This is the SAME ask as GAP-0007 ('Clc 69 and Clc 92') from a different examiner, filed against a different target. Rule 20 prefers a cross-link to an existing owner over duplicating the 1969/1992 history onto a second CLC card - the corpus already carries six CLC-bearing cards.
family_decisions.duplicate_family_note: GAP-0007 and GAP-0684 are the same ask and were never merged in the authorisation.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Say where on board the ship's permitted cargo list is actually found - the list of products appended to the Certificate of Fitness, read with the approved Procedures and Arrangements Manual - and the Annex I equivalent, so the candidate can point to a document rather than describe the categories.
family_decisions.why: The card explains the X/Y/Z/OS categorisation and discharge criteria but never identifies the document that says which cargoes THIS ship may carry, which is the whole ask.
family_decisions.co_author_with: ENR-020 - both turn on what the Certificate of Fitness supplement contains; write them in one sitting so the two cards agree.
family_decisions.target_defect: This card also carries a 'Ship Recycling Sequence' block (IHM Parts I-III, Ship Recycling Plan) inside a MARPOL Annex II card - recorded as debt, not repaired here.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Name the Designated Grievance Redressal Officer in the Indian regime - who holds the post, what grievances go to them, and where they sit in the ladder between the onboard complaint procedure and DGMA - which is the one rung the card's escalation ladder leaves unnamed.
family_decisions.why: The card's ladder runs onboard procedure, company/DPA and flag State, port State control, then external routes, and reaches 'the Indian Shipping Master/DGMA machinery' without ever naming the DGRO the examiner asked for.
family_decisions.target_defect: This card carries a candidate-visible authoring placeholder - '[MS Act 2025 - Part-level, sections pending verification]' - on a live paid page. Recorded as debt; it should be resolved when this edit is made.

family_decisions.missing_limb: Name the shipowner as a distinct duty-holder and say where those duties are stated: MLC Titles 1 to 4 impose them on the shipowner, given effect in India through Part V of the MS Act 2025 - as against the flag and port State duties the card already separates.
family_decisions.why_old_wrong: QB5_D#q3 is the bullying and harassment card. The general question 'responsibility of shipowner towards crew, where is it mentioned' is far broader than harassment and was clustered there only because both touch MLC.
family_decisions.why_new_right: QB4_C#q6 is the MLC structure card. Its second heading is 'Flag State vs. Port State Responsibilities' and the shipowner appears twice in the whole card - the actor who carries most of the MLC's obligations is the one it does not treat.
family_decisions.co_located_with: ENR-039/GAP-0112 now also targets QB4_C#q6 with a different limb - author together, keep the edits distinct.

production_actions.target_q_text: ITC (Institute Time Clauses) — What are the clauses in it?

production_actions.target_q_text: Any incident on your ship

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the distinction between root cause and proximate cause: root cause is the engineering end-point of the RCA the card already performs, while proximate cause is the insurance and legal test of the dominant, effective cause of the loss, and it is proximate cause - not root cause - that decides which policy responds.

production_actions.target_q_text: General Average — Explain including act and procedure followed.

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Say who the average adjuster is and what qualifies them: an independent professional appointed by the shipowner, in practice a Fellow of the Association of Average Adjusters, and why that independence matters to the parties whose contributions they assess.

production_actions.target_q_text: Explain the HNS Convention — to whom does it apply, when does it enter into force, and until then what is the liability/compensation fallback (LLMC limits)?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Explain what the SDR actually is and why the figure moves: an IMF basket unit (USD, EUR, CNY, JPY, GBP), valued daily, with the basket composition and weights reviewed on a fixed multi-year cycle - so a convention limit fixed in SDR is not fixed in any national currency.

production_actions.target_q_text: What does 'clear ground' mean in the context of marine insurance/claims?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Distinguish a marine-insurance warranty from a guarantee: a warranty is a term the assured must comply with exactly, breach of which suspends the insurer's liability from the moment of breach until remedied (Marine Insurance Act 1906 s.33 as reformed by the Insurance Act 2015, which replaced automatic discharge with suspension), whereas a guarantee is a third party's separate promise to answer for performance or defect.

production_actions.target_q_text: ⁠LATEST AMENDMENT IN IMOLEGAL COMMITTEE

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the institutional and commercial response to recent maritime security incidents: the IMO's position and the instruments it has used, the flag State's role and advice to its ships, and the insurance consequence - war-risk listed areas, additional premium on transit, notice to underwriters and crew war-zone entitlements.

production_actions.target_q_text: What is a Contract of Affreightment?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add who carries freight-market risk under a Contract of Affreightment and how: the owner commits tonnage over a period at an agreed rate and so is exposed if the market rises, the shipper secures capacity and is exposed if it falls - which is why a CoA is a hedging instrument as much as a carriage contract.

production_actions.target_q_text: What is a Contract of Affreightment?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Distinguish a plain bareboat/demise charter from a bareboat charter-cum-demise: the latter carries an ownership-transfer obligation at the end of the term, so the periodic payment includes a capital repayment element rather than pure hire - and identify the clause that effects the transfer.

production_actions.target_q_text: Explain the container shipping operational model: what is the difference between Liner, NVOCC, and VOCC, and what are the advantages/disadvantages of each?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the tramp side of the contrast: no fixed schedule or published tariff, employed fixture by fixture under a charterparty rather than a liner bill of lading, freight negotiated per voyage against a market rate, and the different allocation of port, cargo-handling and delay risk that follows.

production_actions.target_q_text: What is Lower Calorific Value? Why is engine performance always quoted against LCV and not the higher value?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the owner's case for an alternative fuel expressed through the card's own quantity: because LCV sets the mass burned per unit of work, a low-carbon fuel's benefit must be stated per unit of ENERGY, not per tonne - and that is what decides bunker cost, tank capacity and compliance value to the owner.

production_actions.target_q_text: Documents related to survey (for CE)

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the class-status ladder the card leaves out: suspension of class - what triggers it (overdue survey, unrectified Condition of Class, unreported casualty), whether it is automatic or discretionary - against withdrawal of class as permanent termination, and the consequence chain from each to statutory certificates, insurance cover and trading.

production_actions.target_q_text: SEQ (Safety Equipment) survey — documents required and how do you prepare for it?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the pre-release controls for sending an LSA item (lifeboat davit / launching appliance) to a shore workshop: use of a maker-authorised or Administration-certificated service provider under MSC.402(96), the scope of work and certification returned, and the evidence the SEQ surveyor expects on completion.

production_actions.target_q_text: Hull survey

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the hull deformation vocabulary a surveyor uses and how each is assessed: buckling, set-in/dishing of plating, tripping of stiffeners and permanent set - what causes each, how the extent is measured against class allowable deformation, and what makes it a Condition of Class.

production_actions.target_q_text: Explain the Enhanced Survey Programme (ESP) — what does it cover and what does the ESP file contain?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Give the ESP its regulatory citation - the SOLAS chapter and the ESP Code resolution that make it mandatory - which is the one part of this four-part ask the card does not answer.

production_actions.target_q_text: What criteria must an organisation meet to become a Recognised Organisation (RO) under IMO/Flag State delegation?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Separate what a class society does as class from what it does as a Recognised Organisation: classification work needs no delegation, whereas statutory certification is exercised only to the extent a particular flag has delegated it in its written RO agreement - so a single society's authority differs flag by flag, and some flags withhold specific certificates entirely.

production_actions.target_q_text: Explain the IMO Goal-Based Standards (GBS) framework — the five-tier hierarchy and its scope of application.

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the objectives half of the ask - why GBS was needed at all: IMO wanted to set and audit the safety goal rather than write construction rules itself, after prescriptive rules alone proved unable to prevent structural losses, so Tier III audit of class rules replaces IMO rule-writing.

production_actions.target_q_text: ICOF — full name, who issues, contents, validity, and survey cycle.

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Enumerate what the ICOF supplement carries besides the list of cargoes: the ship type assignment, the tank-by-tank record of the containment and handling equipment fitted, and the carriage conditions each listed cargo depends on.

production_actions.target_q_text: MARPOL Annex II — contents and certificates required?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Say where on board the ship's permitted cargo list is actually found - the list of products appended to the Certificate of Fitness, read with the approved Procedures and Arrangements Manual - and the Annex I equivalent, so the candidate can point to a document rather than describe the categories.

production_actions.target_q_text: What is a Loadicator, and what are the latest regulatory requirements/amendments concerning it?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the two limbs the card lacks: the item-by-item scope of SOLAS Chapter XII beyond Reg 11 (what the chapter as a whole imposes on bulk carriers), and the stability criteria that must be satisfied after flooding, which the card names as a loadicator output without ever stating.

production_actions.target_q_text: State the Damage Stability Criteria for cargo ships under SOLAS 2009 amendments. What is A ≥ R?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: State why the margin line sat where it did - 76 mm below the bulkhead deck at side as a deliberate reserve against progressive flooding over the bulkhead deck and loss of the evacuation route - so the candidate can explain the principle rather than only report that the 2009 amendments deleted it.

production_actions.target_q_text: IGC Code — explain Type A, B, and C tanks and membrane tanks: shape of each, which is self-supporting, and which has more carrying capacity.

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Draw the IGC/IGF boundary and say which instrument governs a gas-fuelled conversion: IGC governs the ship carrying the gas as CARGO, IGF governs the ship using low-flashpoint gas as FUEL - so a fossil-to-methane main engine retrofit on an LPG carrier is an IGF Code matter even though the ship is an IGC ship.

production_actions.target_q_text: What are the requirements for a container securing arrangement, and what is a Safe Access Plan on a container ship?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: State what actually caps on-deck tier height, since the candidate's 'as per the loading and bay plan' answer names the output rather than the rule: the CSM's approved stack height and stack weight limits, lashing and twistlock capacity, wind heeling and stability, and the navigating-bridge line-of-sight requirement - with the bay plan as the result of those limits.

production_actions.target_q_text: Can you carry timber/log deck cargo on your vessel, and what precautions are taken?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the Load Line timber deck cargo numeric criteria the card omits - the permitted extent and height of the deck stow and the reckoning point used in the timber freeboard assignment - so the candidate can answer with figures rather than with the general TDC Code stability criteria the card already gives.

production_actions.target_q_text: What do the FSS Code and FTP Code contain?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Explain that 'A' is the division class and the number is its insulation rating in minutes: an A-class division is steel or equivalent, suitably stiffened, capable of preventing the passage of smoke and flame for a 60-minute standard fire test, while the A-60/A-30/A-15/A-0 suffix states how long insulation holds the unexposed face within the permitted temperature rise - so A-0 is still an A division with no insulation requirement.

production_actions.target_q_text: CO₂ bottle pressure testing — what is the regime?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the contents-verification and pressure limbs the card omits: how a CO2 cylinder is checked by weighing against its stamped tare weight and the loss that triggers refilling, why that differs from the ultrasonic liquid-level method the examiner contrasted it with, the stored pressure at reference temperature expressed in Pa as asked, and the low-pressure/leak alarm arrangement.

production_actions.target_q_text: Li-ion battery fire on a container vessel — thermal runaway mechanism and CE's actions.

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add what AVD actually is and how it works: an aqueous dispersion of exfoliated vermiculite that, applied to a burning cell, leaves a non-conductive ceramic-like encapsulating layer which cools, isolates and blocks cell-to-cell propagation - and how it is applied relative to the boundary cooling the card already prescribes.

production_actions.target_q_text: What is the carbon conversion factor for HFO and methanol? Calculate CO₂ emitted for one day's fuel consumption.

missing_limbs.missing_limb: State the MGO/MDO carbon factor and explain the counter-intuitive part the examiner was probing: why the distillate's Cf (about 3.206) is HIGHER than HFO's (3.114) even though MGO is the cleaner fuel - because Cf tracks carbon mass fraction, and HFO's sulphur, ash and asphaltenes dilute its carbon per tonne.

production_actions.target_q_text: What is carbon footprint, and how do you check the carbon footprint of your ship?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the GHG Protocol Scope 1/2/3 decomposition and map it onto the boundary distinction the card already draws: Scope 1 direct emissions from fuel burned on board, Scope 2 purchased energy such as shore power, Scope 3 the value chain including upstream fuel production - and note that Scope 1/2/3 is corporate accounting whereas tank-to-wake versus well-to-wake is regulatory accounting.

production_actions.target_q_text: What is a dual fuel engine and a tri-fuel engine? Alarms, monitoring vs conventional engine? LPG bunkering procedures?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the operator-initiated fuel-mode changeover procedure in both directions - gas to diesel and diesel to gas - including the purge and ramp sequence and what must be confirmed before and after, as distinct from the automatic 40 percent LEL trip the card already describes.

production_actions.target_q_text: Compare methane slip control between the MAN ME-GA (Otto-cycle, two-stroke) engine and low-pressure Otto-cycle 4-stroke dual-fuel engines.

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the ME-GI as the missing member of the comparison: high-pressure direct gas injection on the diesel cycle, contrasted with the ME-GA's low-pressure Otto-cycle admission - and how combustion actually proceeds in each, which is what makes their methane-slip behaviour differ.

production_actions.target_q_text: Azimuth propeller — working principle.

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the electric propulsion drive train the azimuth pod hangs off: generator sets to main switchboard, transformer, frequency converter, propulsion motor and pod - and why diesel-electric is chosen for this arrangement.

production_actions.target_q_text: NOx Technical File — what is it, what does it contain, and what does the surveyor check?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Say where an approved component's identification is physically found on the part (the stamped/engraved component number on the cylinder liner and equivalent marking on other listed components) and who issues that number - the engine maker, recorded in the approved components list, which the surveyor matches part-to-file.

production_actions.target_q_text: Moving from Second Engineer to Chief Engineer — what training and certificates does STCW require, and which requirements are national rather than STCW?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the rung below the one the card starts at: the STCW Regulation III/1 entry requirements for an engineer officer of the watch - the qualifying supervised watchkeeping sea service and the 750 kW propulsion-power threshold - so the ladder up to the III/2 3,000 kW certificate the card already explains is complete.

production_actions.target_q_text: TEAP — What is It and Why is It Required?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the qualifying sea service TEAP requires for an engineer officer to sit for and obtain each level of CoC - the national sea-service rule the card's own framework exists to set out.

production_actions.target_q_text: Differentiate between a Certificate of Competency (CoC) and a Certificate of Proficiency (CoP).

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add how a CoP is actually obtained, as against what it is: the approved training and assessment route, who may issue or endorse it, the evidence the Administration requires, and which CoPs carry a refresher obligation.

production_actions.target_q_text: MLC 2006 — 5 Titles and flag/port state duties?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Put figures behind the promise the card already makes: MLC Title 3 accommodation minima - berth internal dimensions, headroom, floor area per seafarer and door sill/coaming heights - as numbers a candidate can quote.

production_actions.target_q_text: MLC 2006 — 5 Titles and flag/port state duties?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Name the shipowner as a distinct duty-holder and say where those duties are stated: MLC Titles 1 to 4 impose them on the shipowner, given effect in India through Part V of the MS Act 2025 - as against the flag and port State duties the card already separates.

production_actions.target_q_text: seafarer ms act welfare requirement

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the Indian seafarer welfare funding institutions the card omits - the Seamen's Provident Fund and the seafarers' welfare fund/board machinery, who contributes and what they pay for - and the COVID-era relief measures taken for stranded and repatriated seafarers.

production_actions.target_q_text: What ship certificates and documents relate to WHO (World Health Organization) requirements?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Bring the Seafarer Medical Fitness Certificate section up to date: state the current medical examination standard and certificate validity position, and the most recent change to it beyond the gender-marker change the examiner set aside.

production_actions.target_q_text: What are your responsibilities and what do you check when taking over as Chief Engineer on a new vessel?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add what changes when the handover is a change of MANAGEMENT rather than a change of chief engineer, scoped to a single intended voyage: no outgoing chief to hand over from, an unverified PMS and defect history, the DOC and SMS transition and interim certification, and how you triage what must be proved before that one voyage as against what can follow.

production_actions.target_q_text: As per the Safety Management System, how is planned maintenance carried out onboard? What does the SMS require?

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the maintenance-type taxonomy the card never names - planned/preventive, corrective/breakdown, condition-based and predictive, and where risk-based maintenance of critical equipment sits - so the candidate can answer 'type of maintenance' rather than describe only the PMS workflow.

missing_limbs.missing_limb: Add the human-element escalation ladder as a graded sequence - counselling and informal correction, formal warning and disciplinary action under the company procedure, and targeted retraining - and state what determines which rung is right.

batches.title: Marine insurance, liability and commercial
batches.rationale: Insurance principles, liability conventions and the chartering/commercial asks. Verification is dominated by market clause wording and convention text.

batches.title: Class, survey, structure and statutory certification
batches.rationale: The class/survey spine plus the two loading-and-stability limbs that share its class-rule verification regime.

batches.title: Cargo, codes and safety systems
batches.rationale: Cargo carriage codes and the fire/LSA system limbs. Smaller batch: every action carries a numeric or code-boundary claim needing primary verification.
